# Chiambucket, Braven Chiam

> Braven Chiam is an Electronic and Computer Engineering student in Singapore. His projects usually combine hardware (circuit boards, sensors, microcontrollers), software (firmware, web apps, servers) and design (3D-printed cases, interfaces). He also photographs the places he travels to and runs a self-hosted homelab. "Chiambucket" is his personal website.

## About Braven
- Year 3 Electronic & Computer Engineering student at Nanyang Polytechnic (NYP), Singapore. Diploma 2024 to 2027, Director's List (Y2S1).
- Most projects are split on the site into the hardware, software and design work he did on each.
- Engineering: microcontrollers (ESP32, Arduino, ATmega328), custom PCB design (KiCAD, EAGLE), 3D CAD (Onshape, Blender), embedded firmware (PlatformIO, C/C++). Mostly self-taught.
- Wireless: LoRa (point-to-point), ESP-NOW, MQTT, WebRTC, SocketIO, 5G cellular.
- Design: UI/interface design (Figma), posters and graphics (Photoshop), video (DaVinci Resolve, Premiere Pro), slide design (PowerPoint), 3D (Spline, Blender).
- Infrastructure: Proxmox, Docker, Nginx, Tailscale, Wireguard, Cloudflare, Unifi.
- Experience: macOS (4 years), Windows (10 years, including Windows Server), Linux (Debian, Ubuntu, Mint, UnRAID).
- Based in Singapore. Email: braven@chiambucket.com. Phone: +65 9710 0366.
- The site is built with Next.js 16 (React 19) and hosted on Vercel.

## Key pages
- [Home](https://www.chiambucket.com/): a scroll story in chapters: who Braven is and the layers he builds in (firmware, hardware, software, infrastructure, design), the OCR Reader as a scroll-driven 3D model of its real board and case ending in its project card, Project June and BeadReader cards, a gallery of the other projects with summaries, recent work "on the bench", a bento of what he does, the homelab drawn in ASCII, a wall of photos and contact.
- [Contact](https://www.chiambucket.com/contact): email (braven@chiambucket.com) and social links.
- [Photography](https://www.chiambucket.com/photography): galleries including Highlights, Europe, China, New Zealand, Hong Kong, 21:9 and General.
- [HomeLab](https://www.chiambucket.com/homelab): A three-node self-hosted homelab that also runs the MQTT and TURN servers his hardware projects use. NewMain (Unraid) plus a Proxmox PXE cluster (CaCa always on, Adell on demand) run around 38 services behind a segmented UniFi network with VLANs and WPA3-Enterprise RADIUS auth. Services include Immich, Nginx Proxy Manager with CrowdSec, Lychee, Pingvin Share, PairDrop, Fireshare, Tailscale, Shadowsocks, UpStat, Paperless-NGX, coturn and Mosquitto.
- [Credits](https://www.chiambucket.com/credits): colophon. The site was built with Claude (Anthropic) and is hosted on Vercel.
- [Braven's Scale of AI use](https://www.chiambucket.com/ai-use): how Braven uses AI, and the four-level scale (L1 little use, L2 average use, L3 heavy use, L4 entirely AI generated) that labels how much of each project was made with AI tools, with the marks free to download as SVG.

## Projects

Flagship project:
- OCR Reader (WaterSlop): a low-cost, battery-powered vision OCR water meter reader built for NYP Electronic and Computer Engineering. A 693K-parameter neural network pipeline, DrumNet V10 (a DetNet spotter, a RefNet edge refiner and an ensemble of three drum readers with a carry rule), runs entirely on an ESP32-S3 with an OV2640 camera, reads the mechanical drums in about 2 s and sends only the number over LoRaWAN. Training used MeterSim (a simulated meter display), SimGen2 (a synthetic camera) and six AI agents on a shared scheduler over Tailscale and T3 Code. Hardware: a 4-layer KiCad PCB (ESP32-S3 N16R8, Wio-SX1262 LoRa, SHT40, battery management), a toolless 3D-printed enclosure and meter adapter, camera focus tests, and ConfigKing, an M5Stack Cardputer setup console over BLE. Current full-pipeline accuracy is 56 %; the target is 99 %. The article opens as one continuous flow: a scroll-driven 3D PCB and enclosure chapter rendered from the real KiCad and CAD files ends with the reader turning to the meter, showing what its camera sees and taking a photo; a full-screen animated film of the whole DrumNet V10 architecture (spotter, refiner twice, cut, three readers, vote and carry rule) then reads that very photo, with a play bar and fast forward; and the ConfigKing chapter shows the same reading on a photo of the real M5Stack Cardputer and walks the setup steps, playing the key press for each, ending in a touch-and-keyboard simulator of the firmware. The later chapters open with a cover and read top to bottom with callouts on real photos and diagrams. It includes a real-versus-SimGen2 compare slider, the Prototype V2 board and enclosure detail, and the embedded report, and a floating button skips to the end. [Article](https://www.chiambucket.com/waterslop)

Highlighted builds:
- Project June (highlighted hardware build): a 5G rover. An ESP32-S3 with GPS, a 10-axis IMU, ultrasonic, light and DHT11 sensors, a MOSFET motor driver and a 2S3P battery pack he built; three phones on board provide the 5G hotspot and three WebRTC camera feeds through a TURN server; MQTT telemetry and control; operator console designed in Figma with a Spline 3D model. Built in 3 weeks, driven from over 8 km away with about one second of delay. [Article](https://www.chiambucket.com/project-june)
- BeadReader (highlighted software build): a private, invite-only online book reader built with Next.js (App Router), Tailwind v4, Supabase (Postgres + Storage) and Cloudflare R2. Access-code auth (one code = identity, role and explicit-content access), per-reader auto-resume and reading themes, live "reading together" presence with ephemeral wave/notes, an explicit-content gate enforced inside the SQL query, Markdown text books and image webtoons, and a shared reading-stats dashboard with streaks. [Article](https://www.chiambucket.com/beadreader)

Other projects:
- LoRA Messenger: a pair of ESP32 handhelds with text over LoRa and rough 2-way voice over ESP-NOW, on his first PCB (KiCAD, soldered by hand), an Onshape 3D-printed case, dual OLEDs and TP4056 charging. [Article](https://www.chiambucket.com/brolocator)
- LUMEN: an AI voice-controlled smart-room assistant on an ESP32 (MicroPython) with a wake word, INMP441 mic and DHT22/PIR/LDR sensors, paired with a Dockerised FastAPI relay that calls OpenRouter for OpenAI Whisper (speech-to-text) and a DeepSeek LLM that parses speech into one validated JSON command, fanned out to lights/fan/servo/buzzer over MQTT. Notable for fitting streamed audio capture onto a no-PSRAM board with ~33 KB free RAM. NYP IoT Programming. [Article](https://www.chiambucket.com/lumen)
- EMA Smart Home System: a school team project (graded A). Four BeagleBone Black Wireless nodes (climate, bathroom, kitchen energy and fire alarm, intrusion) report to a SocketIO server with a Figma-designed dashboard and a live Spline 3D house. [Article](https://www.chiambucket.com/csdp)
- Pandus Dispenser: his first school project, a 6-part 3D-printed syrup dispenser (Onshape) driven by an Arduino Uno with Python and PyFirmata. [Article](https://www.chiambucket.com/pandus)
- ELEC-F: a school team project. An M5Stack walk-in freezer alarm: a ToF sensor watches the door, a PIR sensor checks for people inside, and a timer sounds the alarm if someone is shut in too long. [Article](https://www.chiambucket.com/elecf)
- Copy Board: a KiCAD recreation of NYP's ATMega328 dev board, with sourced replacement parts and first hands-on reflow soldering.
Recent work (on the bench, November 2026; no write-ups yet):
- Shebang: his own hosting platform. One account for sign-in, static pages, file hosting, short links and a Postgres database per project, reachable through one REST API or one MCP server so coding agents can publish. Next.js 16 and self-hosted Supabase. The MCP client, shebang-mcp, is open source: https://github.com/New-Kringster/shebang-mcp
- Pip (in progress): a desk companion on an M5Stack Tab5 (ESP32-P4) that talks to an AI agent running at home, with several desktops, small applets it can build on request, camera use and tear-free page-flipped animation.
- NCIR thermometer demos: live infrared temperature on M5Stack screens for the NCIR and NCIR 2 sensors; the NCIR 2 firmware talks to the sensor's own I2C register map with no vendor library, on the CoreS3 and the classic Basic from one codebase.
- Flashdeck: a firmware shelf with a browser flasher (ESP Web Tools picks the image built for the connected ESP32 chip); a dependency-free Python server.

- Other projects: Kauli (a product concept rendered in Blender), Series One Light (an ultralight mouse shell, about 20 g), his first website (HTML and CSS), and a Minecraft live map hosted on the homelab.
